doc.title: Dick Hyman interviewed by Monk Rowe, Scottsdale, Arizona, March 4, 1995 [interview 1 of 2]

title: Records for MGM with the harpsichord piano sound
summary: An MGM contract came from imitating a French-popular harpsichord-piano sound, after which he played better material.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Record labels, producers and the business of making albums

blocks.x: Can you tell me something about some of the records you made for MGM? They had some interesting titles.

MGM was a company that I’ve recorded for that wanted me to play like a particular recording that was beginning to be popular in France I remember. And it involved a harpsichord piano, that is a grand piano with staples in the hammers so it gave it a clangy sound. It’s useful actually for a harpsichord, even legitimate harpsichord pieces because it’s much louder than a regular harpsichord. At any rate, that was the sound, and it was a very peculiar, not to say moronic treatment that was required. And that’s how I got a contract with MGM. After a while that kind of music and a couple of albums that I’d rather not hear anymore, ran their course and I began to play better for them.
